rv.q: I, too, think teeth are spectacular, and so is this show.
What stands out about her performance is the clarity of the relationships she creates between each of the characters – not an easy task when you're alone on the stage.
If the play takes a while – too long – to tie together the seemingly unrelated parts of the woman’s life, it ultimately inspires sympathy for her, and even outrage on her behalf.
Unfortunately, despite its kooky characters and provocative themes, Issaq's story lacks bite.
The whole is not more than the sum of its parts.

cn.t: Issaq's quirky solo show about a dental technician with a "spiritual infection" earns mixed reviews. Critics praise her warm, neurotic performance but find the narrative unfocused and cumbersome, though it gains clarity as it progresses.
